text: It may be said that the chapter is only following the usage of ancient narrative, where feeling is rarely reported and feeling or motive is never explained. Some truth may lie in this objection. Yet the narrator elsewhere reports feeling plainly enough: Esau cries out, Jacob is afraid, Joseph weeps. The silence of Genesis 22, therefore, is no accident of manner; the reticence is deliberate, and the narrator knows what he is doing.
